method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Most vulval ulcers in children are aphthous or secondary to systemic infection**, rather than sexually transmitted infection.
claims.source_text: Most vulval ulcers in children are aphthous or secondary to a systemic infection, rather than due to sexually transmitted infections
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinical appearance alone is misleading**; investigations are often required.
claims.source_text: Diagnosis on clinical appearance alone is difficult and investigations are often required … Using clinical appearance alone to diagnose the cause of vulval ulcers is misleading due to overlap and variable disease presentation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ulcers are often very painful** and distressing for the child and family.
claims.source_text: Ulcers are often very painful and can cause anxiety and emotional distress for the child and family
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aphthous ulcers:** common in adolescents, may be multiple and recurrent, linked to systemic symptoms or recent illness.
claims.source_text: Aphthous ulcers Common in adolescents May be multiple and recurrent Associated with systemic symptoms or recent illness
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infectious (non-STI):** HSV by autoinoculation, EBV, CMV, VZV, coxsackie virus, *Mycoplasma*, *Candida albicans*.
claims.source_text: Infectious HSV via autoinoculation, EBV, CMV, VZV, coxsackie virus Mycoplasma, Candida albicans
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **STI — HSV:** common; multiple vesicles progressing to painful or itchy ulcers. **Syphilis:** single painless ulcer.
claims.source_text: Sexually transmitted infections HSV Common Multiple vesicles progressing to painful or itchy ulcers Syphilis Single painless ulcer
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Crohn's disease:** linear lesions and fissures, vulval oedema, GI symptoms. **Behçet disease:** recurrent oral ulcers, painful genital ulcers that scar, eye and skin involvement.
claims.source_text: Crohn’s disease Mixed linear inflammatory lesions and fissures Vulvar oedema GI symptoms Behcet disease Recurrent oral ulcers and systemic symptoms, Aphthous genital ulcers, painful and heal with scarring Eye and skin involvement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drug reactions** (e.g. NSAIDs, metronidazole, paracetamol, sulfonamides, tetracycline, phenytoin, oral contraceptives) have no definitive features. ⚠️ **SJS/TEN:** flu-like illness, mucous membrane and skin ulcers, conjunctivitis.
claims.source_text: Drug reactions NSAIDs, metronidazole, paracetamol, sulfonamides, tetracycline, phenytoin, oral contraceptives, barbiturate, phenolphthalein No definitive features Exposure to medication Stevens-Johnson syndrome/ toxic epidermal necrolysis Flu-like illness Ulcers across mucous membranes and skin Conjunctivitis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** single or multiple, first or recurrent, painful or painless, evolution, **difficulty passing urine**; systemic, GI, respiratory, oral, skin, eye and joint symptoms.
claims.source_text: Single or multiple lesions First episode or recurrent Painful or painless Evolution of ulcer(s) Difficulty passing urine Review of systems: Systemic symptoms: fever, malaise, headache, myalgia Gastrointestinal symptoms Respiratory symptoms Oral ulcers, skin lesions, eye and joint symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about family autoimmune disease and ethnicity** (Behçet is more common in Mediterranean and South East Asian families), skin care, sexual history, and medication or topical product exposure.
claims.source_text: Family history autoimmune disorders and family ethnicity (Behcet disease is more common in families from Mediterranean countries and South East Asia) Normal skin care and hygiene routines Sexual history Medication and topical product (washing detergent, soaps etc) exposure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine:** ulcer size, shape, colour and site; secondary skin changes; oral ulcers; joints and eyes if autoimmune causes are considered; skin for eczema, rash, ulcers or bullae; lymphadenopathy.
claims.source_text: Size, shape, colour, location of vulval ulcers Presence of secondary skin changes (excoriation, lichenification, oedema, crust, bleeding, pigmentation, scar) Oral ulcers Joint and eye examination when autoimmune causes being considered Skin inspection for eczema, rash, other ulcers or bullae Lymphadenopathy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Swab the ulcer:** HSV-1/2 and VZV PCR; Gram stain, culture and syphilis PCR; fungal wet prep and culture.
claims.source_text: Swab ulcer(s): Viral: HSV-1 and 2, VZV PCR Bacterial: Gram stain and culture, syphilis PCR Fungal: wet prep and culture
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider bloods:** serology for HSV-1/2, EBV (plus monospot), CMV, syphilis and *Mycoplasma*; CRP, ESR, FBE, ANA ± HLA-B51 for Behçet.
claims.source_text: Consider blood tests: Serology for HSV-1 and 2, EBV (plus monospot), CMV, Syphilis and Mycoplasma CRP, ESR, FBE, ANA ± HLA-B51 (Behcet)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A non-healing lesion may need biopsy.**
claims.source_text: If non-healing lesion, may need biopsy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Analgesia:** simple oral, and topical (viscous xylocaine, lidocaine gel 2%).
claims.source_text: Analgesia – simple oral, topical (xylocaine viscous, lidocaine gel 2%)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Minimise irritants** (no soaps, pads or tight clothing); **pass urine in a bath or with a spray bottle** to reduce dysuria; salt baths, cool compresses, barrier cream.
claims.source_text: Minimise irritants (no soaps, pads, tight underwear or clothing) Pass urine while using a spray bottle or in a bath to reduce dysuria Salt baths Cool compresses Barrier cream
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If unable to void, admission for a urinary catheter may be required.**
claims.source_text: If unable to void, admission for a urinary catheter may be required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider aciclovir if primary HSV is likely; topical corticosteroids if aphthous ulcers are most likely; antibiotics if bacterial infection is suspected**; treat any STI.
claims.source_text: Antiviral: consider aciclovir if primary HSV is likely diagnosis Steroids: consider topical corticosteroids if aphthous ulcers most likely Antibiotics: if bacterial infection suspected Treat sexually transmitted infections
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** if admission for a urinary catheter is needed.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Admission for urinary catheter is required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Seek gynaecology, dermatology, rheumatology or infectious diseases advice** when the diagnosis is unclear or a more serious cause is a concern.
claims.source_text: Appropriate specialist consultation with gynaecology, dermatology, rheumatology or infectious diseases is required when the diagnosis is unclear or there is concern for a more serious cause
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected sexual assault: follow local guidelines; early specialist consultation is vital.**
claims.source_text: If sexual assault is suspected, please refer to local guidelines. Early consultation with specialist services is vital
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge with adequate symptom relief and a clear follow-up plan.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when: Adequate symptom relief and clear follow up plan in place
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval ulcers' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_ulcers/, retrieved 2026-09-23
